definition: A collection of software tools, libraries, and documentation that simplifies building applications on top of a particular platform or API.
details: SDKs for AI model APIs typically handle authentication, request formatting, response parsing, and error handling, reducing the boilerplate developers need to write to integrate a model into their application.

explainer.lead: A software development kit is a collection of tools, libraries, and documentation that simplifies building applications on a particular platform or API. SDKs matter because they cut the integration work developers must do themselves.

tiers.eli5: It is a ready-made toolbox for building on a platform, so you don't have to make the basic parts yourself.
tiers.practitioner: SDKs for AI model APIs handle authentication, request formatting, response parsing, and error handling, removing boilerplate. A pitfall is coupling: relying on an SDK's conveniences can tie your code to that platform's conventions.
tiers.paperLevel: An SDK bundles software tools, libraries, and documentation that simplify building applications on top of a particular platform or API; for AI model APIs it typically covers authentication, request formatting, response parsing, and error handling.

explainer.example: A developer integrating a model API calls an SDK function that authenticates, sends the request, and parses the response, instead of writing that plumbing by hand.
